label: DrayTek Vigor 2767ax-4G VDSL2 / 2.5GbE Wi-Fi 6 4G router
description: DrayTek Vigor 2767ax-4G - VDSL2/ADSL2+ router with a 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet switchable WAN/LAN port, three Gigabit LAN ports, an integrated 4G/LTE Cat 6 modem with dual nano-SIM and eSIM, and Wi-Fi 6 AX3000 dual-band (574 Mbps at 2.4 GHz, 2402 Mbps at 5 GHz). Up to 2.3 Gbps NAT throughput, 300 Mbps IPsec, 16 VPN tunnels, 4 LAN subnets with 8 VLANs.
notes: The physical-interface block is quoted in full: '**WAN Ports: 1x VDSL2 / ADSL2+, RJ-11**', '**WAN/LAN Switchable Port: 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet (2.5G/1G/100M/10M), RJ-45**', '**LAN Ports: 3x Gigabit Ethernet (1G/100M/10M), RJ-45**'. The page then says '**In total 4 (3+1) LAN ports (1 is the WAN/LAN switchable)**', which is the modelling decision: four RJ-45 sockets, not five. So the spec declares `dsl0`, a 2.5G `wan` and three 1G LAN ports, and a lab that needs four LAN sockets reassigns the 2.5G one - which is exactly what the hardware does. Declaring both a `wan` and four LAN ports would show five sockets on a four-socket box (the same call as the V2765-K and V2766-K). The 4G side is one Cat 6 modem (300 Mbps down / 50 Mbps up) with **two nano-SIM slots and eSIM**, so a single `wwan0` bearer with failover inside it - not four cellular WANs. DrayTek also lists 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz **wireless WAN** as WAN3/WAN4: Wi-Fi as an uplink is a configuration of the radios, not extra sockets, so it lives in this note rather than as a port. Radios are AX3000: 574 Mbps at 2.4 GHz and 2402 Mbps at 5 GHz, both quoted. No PoE anywhere - 12 V supply.
